nodes.question: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

Tighten the criterion to assess the overall rendering medium and degree of transformation against the source, distinguishing a convincingly chalk-made drawing from a photo with chalk-like effects, while preserving the rubric’s partial-progress path when evidence supports some but not complete transformation. Ensure the decision logic does not equate a skipped support with evidence either way; investigate whether s2’s conditional skip is appropriate for this criterion rather than treating its transport-level “unobserved” status as negative visual evidence. The reference label is aggregate guidance, not atomic ground truth, so do not force partial solely to match it; make the visual evidence and completion threshold explicit and calibrated.
s1: The trace’s evidence supports a substantial chalk-like transformation: the edited image has a visibly grainy, softened, smudged rendering, while retaining the source scene and recognizable giraffes. But those cues alone do not establish that the image as a whole convincingly reads as a chalk drawing; the node’s pass criterion and binding should distinguish an overall medium transformation from texture effects layered onto a still-photographic image. Make the criterion assess the image globally and compare its rendering to the source, while allowing partial progress when the requested style is clearly applied but completion remains uncertain. Calibrate confidence to that distinction rather than treating one high-confidence support pass as proof of full fulfillment. Keep unavailable-image or execution/transport failures unresolved, not negative visual evidence; do not infer anything from a skipped check or force the aggregate reference label as atomic truth.
